thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [AUTO] High error-rate detected for continuous-batcher pool 'cb-eu-1' (5m avg error-rate: 18%). Potential KV cache growth spike.

alex: saw the bot. spike started ~1801012200. latency also climbing for a handful of customers.

sre_jordan: on it. taking lead for triage. can someone post recent config for continuous batching? suspect misconfig.

ops_ana: attaching the runtime config we pushed this morning to cb-eu-1:```
continuous_batch:
  max_batch_tokens: 10000000
  max_num_seqs: 1024
  timeout_ms: 1000
  kv_cache_enabled: true
```

mia: whoops. that max_batch_tokens looks... wild. I thought we rolled a conservative change (10k) but appears a customer override landed with an extra zero?

eng-runtime-kevin: confirmed: there's an override for customer tenant 'shopmate-prod' that set max_batch_tokens=10000000 via the runtime policy API at 1801012105. That will cause very large per-batch token allocations and KV cache entries.

alex: ok, what's the immediate mitigation? are customers impacted or just internal errors?

customer-success-raj: CX reported 3 paying customers seeing degraded response times and intermittent 502s. I have their accounts and org IDs if needed.

sre_jordan: plan: 1) throttle the offending tenant by immediately applying a lower per-tenant cap 2) reduce cluster-wide max_batch_tokens to safe value 3) restart continuous-batcher pods gradually 4) monitor KV cache size and OOMs.

oncall-rotation: I can apply the tenant throttle and coordinate restarts. Who has admin to push config?

eng-runtime-kevin: I do. applying tenant patch now.

eng-runtime-kevin: ```bash
# runtime admin API (internal)
curl -X POST https://runtime-admin.internal/configs/tenant/shopmate-prod \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"continuous_batch":{"max_batch_tokens":5120,"max_num_seqs":32}}'
```

eng-runtime-kevin: patch applied at 1801012360. tenant throttle in effect.

ops_ana: also setting cluster default to safer values to prevent other tenants inheriting crazy values.```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap continuous-batcher --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_batch_tokens":"5120","max_num_seqs":"64","timeout_ms":"500"}}'
```

alex: rolling restart to pick up config? safe to restart all pods? want to avoid mass reconnects.

sre_jordan: doing a staggered restart across availability zones. 25% at a time. command:```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/continuous-batcher --selector=zone=eu-west-1 --timeout=600s
```

mia: note: since KV cache lives in-process, we expect cache sizes to shrink as new batches are limited. but there may be a short-term memory pressure as stale large entries evict. watch for OOMs.

eng-runtime-kevin: restart started at 1801012400. first wave healthy.

sre_jordan: monitoring metrics: KV cache size dropped ~60% after first wave. error-rate trending down.

customer-success-raj: customers reported improvements ~2m after restart. still collecting final confirmations from two orgs.

alex: what caused the bad override to land? is this user error or bug?

eng-runtime-kevin: root cause appears to be missing validation on the tenant config endpoint. we accepted unbounded integers. UI/cli allowed a pasted value with extra zero.

mia: we should block max_batch_tokens > 100k at API layer and add server-side clamps.

sre_jordan: agreed. short-term mitigation: add a hard cap in the runtime proxy so any incoming runtime-config > 200k gets clamped. I'll open a hotfix.

eng-runtime-kevin: hotfix PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/3142 (deploying to canary now).

ops_ana: canary passed. deploying to prod at 1801012620.

sre_jordan: after deploy and final restarts, error-rate back to baseline ~0.6% and tail latency normalized. KV cache growth no longer observed.

alex: customer impact summary for incident report: 3 customers impacted, intermittent 502s and elevated latency for ~20-40 minutes depending on region; no data loss. CX engaged.

customer-success-raj: submitted support notes to affected accounts and scheduled follow-ups. all asked for postmortem.

mia: follow-up actions (for postmortem):
- add server-side limits for continuous_batch config values
- UI validation and warnings for tenant overrides
- alert rule for anomalous per-tenant max_batch_tokens changes
- add unit/integration test covering large values causing KV cache growth
- consider autoscaling strategy if large tenants cause cache pressure

eng-runtime-kevin: deploying the validation hotfix across regions. also adding telemetry that logs tenant-config diffs to S3 for audit.

sre_jordan: tagging incident for oncall handoff. oncall-rotation will take post-deploy watch window.

oncall-rotation: taking handoff. I'll watch metrics for next 2 hours and escalate if anything creeps back. :eyes:

alex: thanks team. please label this thread with #incident and link the postmortem when ready.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: #INC-2026-1801012345. Timeline and actions captured.

eng-runtime-kevin: PR for validation merged. reference: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/commits/8a7f2c

mia: adding postmortem owner and tentative due date: 1801070000 (1 week).

sre_jordan: closing handoff. great quick work. :thumbsup:
